name: James
overview: James was a male disciple of the Messiah and one of the Twelve apostles, as identified in Matthew 10:3. Though his tribal affiliation is not recorded, he is distinguished by his role as a close follower of Jesus Christ during His earthly ministry.
namesAndTitles: The name James means 'follower, replacer, one who follows at the heel,' reflecting a Hebrew/Greek meaning associated with discipleship. He is also referred to as Levi in Mark 2:14, though no specific meaning is given for this name in the provided facts.
familyAndRelationships: James is explicitly recorded as the son of Alphaeus and a disciple and apostle of YHVH, according to Matthew 10:3. Beyond these relationships, Scripture does not provide additional family details for him in the given data.
scriptureSignificance: James holds a significant place in the biblical narrative as a devoted apostle and disciple of Christ, one of the Twelve chosen to follow Jesus. His life demonstrates the necessity of personal faith, even among those close to Jesus, as he came to faith fully after the resurrection. He is recognized for his leadership in the early church and for authoring an epistle that emphasizes the practical outworking of genuine faith through good works, complementing the teachings of Paul.
